title: WebMCP Attack Lab: Can an E-Shop Hijack Your AI Agent?
why_read: A concrete, hands-on demonstration of a prompt-injection-style attack against WebMCP, a new standard letting AI agents interact directly with web pages, which is a timely and practical security concern.
analysis: The author builds a demo e-commerce site using Angular's experimental WebMCP support and shows how a malicious shop could manipulate an AI shopping agent's tool descriptions to make it ignore a user's budget constraints. This is a practical, reproducible exploration of a real emerging attack surface, since WebMCP is designed specifically to let agents take actions like adding to cart and checking out on a user's behalf. It builds on the author's earlier related work on prompt injection via log files, showing a consistent interest in adversarial testing of agentic AI systems. This kind of hands-on red-teaming is valuable for engineers building or integrating AI agents into web-facing products.
